questions.q: What does Covey call the greatest gift we are born with?
a: The freedom to choose how we respond
The ability to learn new skills quickly
The capacity to remember the past
The talent for influencing other people
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we cannot control events, only our reaction to them.

questions.q: Which four kinds of intelligence does the summary list?
a: Physical, mental, emotional and spiritual
Logical, creative, social and practical
Mental, emotional, financial and physical
Spiritual, artistic, verbal and spatial
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes these as the powers behind finding your voice.

questions.q: Which three behaviors does the summary say build trust?
a: Keeping promises, being kind and apologizing sincerely
Working hard, staying quiet and taking blame
Being honest, dressing well and arriving early
Sharing credit, staying neutral and avoiding errors
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists following through, friendliness and prompt apologies.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest empowering employees?
a: Give them control over decisions about their own work
Give them more tasks without more authority
Praise them publicly but keep decisions central
Rotate them through every department quickly
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses a cleaning crew choosing its own tools and schedule.

questions.q: What does the summary say about individual productivity in the Information Age?
a: A top knowledge worker can be far more valuable than an average one
Physical strength still determines most workplace output
Individual differences in output are now marginal
Teamwork matters less as knowledge work grows
questions.why: The overview contrasts the Industrial Age's marginal differences with today's knowledge work.
